purpose: This medication is used to treat certain types of breast cancer and stomach cancer that have a protein called HER2 on the cancer cells. It helps slow down or stop the growth of these cancers. It can be used alone or together with other cancer medicines.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have too many of a protein called HER2, which tells the cancer to grow quickly. This medicine works like a guided missile — it finds and attaches to that HER2 protein on the cancer cells. Once attached, it blocks the signal that tells the cancer to grow and also helps your immune system attack those cancer cells.
common_side_effects: Feeling tired, nausea, diarrhea, headache, fever, chills, rash, joint or muscle pain, and low white blood cell counts. Some people feel flu-like symptoms during or after the infusion, such as chills, fever, and body aches.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious heart problems, including heart failure — your doctor will monitor your heart regularly. It can cause severe infusion reactions, so you will be watched carefully during each treatment. It should NOT be used during pregnancy as it can harm your unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you have shortness of breath, swelling in your legs, or chest pain.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an IV infusion (through a vein) by a healthcare provider, usually once every 1 to 3 weeks depending on your treatment plan. The first dose is given slowly over about 90 minutes, and if tolerated well, later doses may be given over 30 minutes. Your doctor will decide the exact dose based on your weight and treatment schedule.
